title: Derived tensor preserves locally constant finite type cohomology
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B$ a commutative Noetherian ring. If $K,L\in D^-(\mathcal C,\underline B)$ have all cohomology sheaves locally constant of finite type, then every cohomology sheaf of $K\otimes_B^L L$ is locally constant of finite type. Here constants are [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], derived categories and cohomology are [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and Noetherian means [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; locally constant of finite type means locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finitely generated module. No existence of points of the site is assumed. Here $D^-$ denotes objects whose cohomology vanishes in sufficiently high degrees, and $K\otimes_B^L L$ denotes the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] after replacing the factors by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex].

proof.text: Work on the slice [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] over an arbitrary object $U$; it has final object $U$. Restriction is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], hence commutes with cohomology and good truncations. It commutes with sheaf tensor: from [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the two presheaf tensor formulas agree at each object over $U$, and sheafification on that slice gives the same local sections and local relations. It preserves flat sheaves: for an exact sequence on the slice apply the exact $j_{U!}$, tensor with a flat sheaf upstairs, use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor], and reflect exactness through $j_{U!}$. To justify this reflection, $j_{U!}$ detects zero sheaves: a nonzero section of $F$ over an object with specified map to $U$ gives a section in that summand of the extension-by-zero presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]; by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], it can become zero in its sheafification only if it is locally zero, which also makes the original section zero. Thus the exact functor $j_{U!}$ detects zero homology objects, hence reflects exactness. No identity $j_U^*j_{U!}=1$ is claimed. Thus bounded-above flat representatives stay bounded-above flat, and are K-flat on each slice by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Their total tensor also restricts termwise, so derived tensor and its cohomology can be computed on these slices.

source.place: Tag 094H: local computation; Tag 06YS: bounded-above K-flat representatives

proof.text: Fix a degree $i$, and upper cohomological bounds $b_K,b_L$. For an upper bound $b$, replace degree $b$ of a representing complex by the kernel of its outgoing differential and all higher terms by zero. The inclusion preserves cohomology in degrees at most $b$, and both cohomologies vanish above $b$, so it is a quasi-isomorphism; [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] and [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] give flat K-flat representatives with those same term bounds. More generally, objects with bounds $c,d$ have derived tensor with zero cohomology above $c+d$, since every summand in total degree $n>c+d$ vanishes. Put $a_K=i-b_L$, $a_L=i-b_K$. The lower truncation replaces degree $a_K$ by the cokernel of its incoming differential, keeps higher terms, and sets lower terms to zero; the outgoing differential descends since $d^2=0$. The natural map $K\to K_0=\tau_{\geq a_K}K$ induces an isomorphism on degree-$i$ tensor cohomology with $L$. Indeed its kernel on a representative is quasi-isomorphic to $\tau_{<a_K}K$, whose tensor with $L$ has upper bound $(a_K-1)+b_L=i-1$. Tensor the termwise short exact truncation sequence with the flat representative of $L$; exactness follows from the definition [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and finite direct sums in each total degree. The kernel has zero cohomology in degrees $i,i+1$. Local lifts and local equality in quotient sheaves follow from [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] applied to the corresponding quotient presheaves. Explicitly, locally lift a degree-$i$ cycle of the quotient to the middle complex: its differential is a kernel cycle in degree $i+1$, hence locally a boundary; subtract its kernel primitive to obtain a cycle lift. If a middle cycle becomes a boundary in the quotient, locally lift a quotient primitive and subtract its differential; the remaining kernel cycle in degree $i$ is locally a boundary. These two local chases give surjectivity and injectivity of the cohomology-sheaf map, hence the asserted isomorphism. K-flatness makes its tensor cohomology independent of a replacement of that kernel: the cone [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of a quasi-isomorphism is acyclic (by the same cycle/boundary chase), and tensoring it with the K-flat representative of L is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The signed total tensor of that cone is the cone of the tensor map, as is checked on its two summands. Thus the tensor map is a quasi-isomorphism. Repeating with $L\to L_0=\tau_{\geq a_L}L$ and the bound $b_K$ of $K_0$ gives $H^i(K\otimes_B^L L)\cong H^i(K_0\otimes_B^L L_0)$. Both truncated objects are bounded and keep the required cohomology sheaves. If a lower cutoff exceeds its upper bound, that truncated object is zero and the same argument applies.

source.place: Tag 094H, first two sentences of proof; corrected lower cutoffs depending on upper bounds

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-bounded-constant-model] to $K_0$ on $\mathcal C/U$. On each resulting slice apply it to $L_0$ as well and compose the two covering families, obtaining simultaneous models $\underline{E^\bullet}$ and $\underline{F^\bullet}$ with $E,F$ bounded complexes of finite $B$-modules. This only uses a finite number of covering refinements for the fixed degree $i$, not a common covering for infinitely many cohomological degrees. Zero objects can be represented by the zero complex.

source.place: Tag 094H: application of Tag 094G on slices

proof.text: The constant-module functor is exact and commutes with cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], applied to constant presheaf complexes. Cohomology of the bounded finite-module complexes $E,F$ is finite: for a submodule $N\subset B^r$, project onto the last coordinate. Its image is a finitely generated ideal by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], its kernel is finite by induction on $r$, and lifts of image generators together with kernel generators generate $N$. For a submodule of a finite module take its preimage under $B^r\twoheadrightarrow M$ and project generators. Kernels, images and their quotients in $E,F$ are therefore finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] these complexes are pseudo-coherent, and [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] supplies bounded-above finite free models $P,Q$. Exactness of the constant functor sends their derived isomorphisms (represented by roofs of quasi-isomorphisms) to derived isomorphisms. Each $\underline{P^p}$ is a finite sum of copies of $\underline B$, and tensoring with it is a finite sum of the identity functor, so it is flat; similarly for $Q$. Thus [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes $\underline P,\underline Q$ K-flat representatives of the two objects.

source.place: Tag 094H: replace the constant finite-module complexes by bounded-above finite free models; Tag 066E

proof.text: On such a covering slice the tensor is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(\underline P\otimes_{\underline B}\underline Q)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For free modules with bases, the tensor basis identifies $\underline{B^r}\otimes_{\underline B}\underline{B^s}$ with $\underline{B^{rs}}$: the maps send basis tensors to basis vectors and conversely; they are inverse by bilinearity. This is the sheafified tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. If $P^p=0$ for $p>c$ and $Q^q=0$ for $q>d$, total degree $n$ has only the finitely many summands $n-d\leq p\leq c$, $q=n-p$. Consequently the total complex is the termwise constant complex of the bounded-above finite free $B$-complex $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_B Q)$, with differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] its degree-$i$ cohomology is $\underline{H^i(T)}$. This module is finite by the submodule argument in Step 4. Therefore that cohomology sheaf is constant of finite type on the covering slice.

source.place: Tag 094H, final sentence: finite free tensor calculation

proof.text: For the arbitrary object $U$ and degree $i$, Steps 2 and 3 identify the restriction of $H^i(K\otimes_B^L L)$ on a covering of $U$ with the constant finite-module sheaf computed in Step 5. This is precisely the local constant finite-type condition in the statement. Letting $U$ and $i$ vary proves every required cohomology sheaf has the property; no stalks, points, or simultaneous infinite covering refinement were used.
